10.0.s.en: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

10.0.0.en: St. Paul means by “the fathers” the Israelites who went out with Moses from the land of Egypt. The cloud is the one that covered them and guided them as they moved through the wilderness of Sinai, and the sea is the Red Sea, which was divided into two halves and through the midst of which they crossed.

10.1.0.en: The inspired Word counted their going down into the depths of the sea, and the cloud covering them, as being immersed under the water, that is, as being baptized; and because Moses was their leader in this crossing, this baptism was ascribed to him.

10.2.0.en: All the children of Israel shared in eating the manna, a symbol of Holy Communion, which the Lord gave them miraculously from heaven; therefore it was called spiritual food.

10.3.0.en: Likewise all of them shared in drinking the water of the rock that Moses caused to burst forth in the wilderness, and because this too happened miraculously, it was also called spiritual drink.

10.3.1.en: As for the rock following them, there is a Jewish tradition which says that the rock rolled along behind them wherever they went, with water coming out of it, or that a stream of water came out of it and followed them on their journey in the wilderness. The rock is a symbol of Christ, because He was a support to them, quenching their thirst and caring for them.

10.4.0.en: In spite of the many gifts God had bestowed on them, all the adults among them, except Joshua and Caleb, angered the Lord by their misconduct, their disobedience and their worship of idols, so He caused them to die in the wilderness and they did not enter the Promised Land.

10.5.0.en: God intended these events to be a lesson and a warning for us, besides being a punishment for the Israelites for their sins. Here St. Paul warns the believers of Corinth against committing sins like those that prevented the Israelites from entering the Promised Land, lest they be deprived of entering heaven.

10.6.0.en: Our teacher St. Paul refers here to the incident mentioned in the Book of Numbers (Num 25:1-9), when the daughters of Moab invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to the idols, and then the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab, so the Lord caused them to die by a plague that cut down 23,000 of them. (The Book of Numbers mentions that those who died were 24,000. There is no contradiction in this: in the Book of Numbers the total number of those who died is recorded, whereas in the Epistle to the Corinthians the number of those who died in a single day is recorded, while the plague continued for more than a day.)

10.7.0.en: The Apostle refers here to what happened to the people anciently when the serpents destroyed them as they murmured against the manna (Num 21:5, 6); the Lord sent serpents upon the people, and they bit them, and many of them died. So he warns the believers of Corinth not to tempt Christ as they did, by their murmuring, their disobedience and their seeking of worldly pleasures, and not to expose themselves to evil in order to see whether Christ will rescue them or not.

10.8.0.en: He refers here to the rebellion of Korah and his companions against Moses and their rejection of his authority over them (Num 16); the earth was split open and swallowed them up, and they perished from among the congregation. This is a warning to the Corinthians that if they presume upon God’s gentleness and patience and transgress His commandments, they bring spiritual destruction upon themselves.

10.8.1.en: If God has given you good things, it is natural that you should thank Him for them. Let your outlook be simple, so that you enjoy God’s gifts instead of being distressed by what you lack and murmuring against Him; rather, know that it is by God’s permission, for your benefit. You can ask Him to remove the affliction, and for His help and support.

10.9.0.en: Here is a warning to the believers of Corinth not to be excessively confident in themselves. Their living in a pagan environment exposes them to falling into the sins of the Gentiles, just as happened to the people of old, who, although the Lord had singled them out for special care, rebelled and disobeyed, and so fell into idolatry and fornication, and tempted the Lord and murmured against Him, and thus exposed themselves to the divine wrath.

10.10.0.en: This is the rule that the Corinthians had to learn from the history of the Israelites: that as long as a person is on earth he is liable to fall. So whoever thinks that he is steadfast in faith and godliness should take heed lest he fall into sin, for the one who relies on his own strength is more liable to fall than others.

10.11.0.en: The word temptation in Greek means a test or an examination; so what is meant by temptation is that it is a means of examining and testing the steadfastness of a person’s heart toward God.

10.11.1.en: What is meant by the phrase “such as is common to man” is that these temptations are within the capacity and ability of human beings, who pass through them successfully if they rely on divine grace; for God is faithful in His promises, and never allows us to be exposed to a temptation that is beyond our ability to bear, but gives us strength and ability to pass through it. The way of escape is the means of coming out of the temptation, of sensing God and of regaining inner peace, such as God sending a solution to the problem, or the support of another person, or spiritual benefit from the temptation, so that its weariness is lightened...

10.12.0.en: Paul addressed the Corinthians with the words “my dearly beloved” so that they might be certain that his advice to them came from love for them and concern for their salvation. Here he asks them to keep away from idolatry, from entering the temple of an idol, from eating at their feasts, and indeed from any participation with the pagans in their rites; otherwise they would deprive themselves of the Lord’s help, which would expose them to falling.

10.12.1.en: Be assured that all temptations are by God’s permission, as long as you love Him and walk in His way; and however great your weakness, He will support you to pass through the temptation successfully and benefit from it. However hard it may seem, His divine power will open for you a way of escape from it in a manner beyond your understanding. So thank God at all times for His wonderful works with you.

10.13.s.en: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

10.13.0.en: The Apostle regarded them as wise men, able to see that his words accord with sound reason, and that his forbidding them to eat in the idol’s temple is not merely a desire to impose his apostolic authority upon them, but that there are logical reasons that they can easily understand if they think deeply.

10.14.0.en: The word fellowship in Greek means union. It was called the cup of blessing because it contains the blood of Christ, which was shed on the wood of the Cross. By eating of the bread, which is the Body of Christ, we are united with Him; therefore by partaking of the Body and Blood we become members of the Body of Christ.

10.15.0.en: Our partaking of the bread and the cup means a real union with Christ, for the one body, even though it has many members, remains one.

10.15.1.en: Here is an affirmation of the truth and doctrine of the change of the bread and wine into the Body and Blood of the Lord; otherwise they would not create fellowship and union among those who partake of them. Let us beware of contrary doctrines that make the change dependent only on the faith of those who partake, or that deny this change altogether.

10.16.0.en: Here is a proof, from what was done in the Jewish worship in the temple, of what St. Paul had already established concerning partaking of the Body and Blood of Christ. When the Israelites offered sacrifices to die on their behalf, as the command of the Law required, they believed that they were one with these sacrifices. In this sense, then, they were partakers of the altar. The Jews also used to divide the sacrifice and eat it among themselves, and no one could enter the temple and share with those present in eating the sacrifice unless he acknowledged that he was a Jew, united with them, worshipping with them the one God.

10.17.0.en: Whoever takes part in offering a sacrifice to idols, or eats of it believing that it is offered to the idol, declares his faith in, and his fellowship in, the worship of this idol. The worship of idols gladdens Satan because it draws people away from the true God; therefore whoever offers sacrifices to an idol is united and associated with the demons. And I do not want this fate for you, which would take you far from God.

10.18.0.en: A person cannot be a partaker in a thing and its opposite, just as it is impossible for light to be united with darkness. You cannot partake of the Lord’s Supper in a way that pleases God and profits your souls while you go to the temple of the idol, which is Satan, and take part in its feasts. Eating of what is offered to Satan will stand as a barrier between you and union with the Lord. But whoever eats of what was sacrificed to idols, not to please them but as a gift from God, does no wrong, because he believes not in the idols but in God alone, while taking care not to cause the stumbling of any of those who understand that eating the meat is honoring the idol and worshipping it (ch. 8:4).

10.19.0.en: Jealousy belongs to the nature of a man if his wife betrays him and loves someone other than him. The books of the Old Testament spoke of the turning of the people of old to idolatry as spiritual adultery, and of Israel as the bride of the Lord. God expressed His anger as jealousy, as stated in (Deut 32:21 and Ps 78:

10.19.1.en: 58.) The question here expresses astonishment at the folly of the Christians who provoke God’s wrath by attending pagan feasts.

10.19.2.en: Paul’s second question, “are we stronger than he?”, is a rhetorical question, for we are in no way stronger than the Lord. It is not permissible for Christians, who are the bride of Christ (Eph 5:25-31), to provoke the Lord’s jealousy by sharing in the table of demons.

10.19.3.en: As long as we partake of the Holy Sacraments, it is not fitting for us to attend parties that please Satan because of the dancing, drinking of wine, songs and arousing of desires in them, such as the parties held after the sacrament of marriage is completed in the church. How can we be united with God and Satan at the same time?

10.19.4.en: (4) Freedom and causing others to stumble (vv. 23-33, ch. 11:1:) 23 All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. 24 Let no man seek his own, but every man another’s wealth. 25 Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience’ sake: 26 for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof. 27 If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go, whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience’ sake. 28 But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience’ sake: for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof: 29 conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man’s conscience? 30 For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks? 31 Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God. 32 Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Greeks, nor to the church of God: 33 even as I please all men in all things, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.

10.19.5.en: Ch. 11:1 Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

10.20.0.en: This repeats what was previously explained in (ch. 6:12), that Christian freedom is not absolute. When we were united with Christ, our aim became to please Him and to keep away from evil, from whatever causes others to stumble, and from everything that is unprofitable or unedifying, such as excess in eating and drinking, or being in places that are not fitting for the children of God, or wearing clothes that draw attention; likewise any useless talk, or wasting time in fruitless occupations.

10.21.0.en: The believer must prefer the benefit of others to his own personal pleasure, even if what he does is sound and pure but causes the weak to stumble; so he forgets his own comfort and mood and seeks the comfort of others.

10.22.0.en: Whatever is sold in the meat markets, eat of it without asking whether it was sacrificed to an idol or not, because by this question you expose your consciences to stumbling and doubt.

10.23.0.en: For the Lord God is the Creator of the earth and all that is in it of fruits and animals; all of it is God’s, and He has made it food for man, and there is no need for doubts and debate over whether to eat it or not.

10.24.0.en: If you wish to accept an invitation from unbelievers to eat with them, and you are willing to accept their invitation, there is no objection to your eating what is set before you, on condition that you do not ask whether it is from the sacrifices of idols or not, so that you do not burden your consciences.

10.25.0.en: But if one of those invited with you, one of the brethren weak in faith, tells you that this is sacrificed to an idol, because he imagines that it is forbidden, then if you eat you wound his conscience. So do not eat of it, out of regard for his weak conscience, even if you are convinced that it is clean because it is from the hand of God and your conscience did not rebuke you for eating it, because there is no reason to refrain from the food except to avoid causing the believing brother to stumble.

10.26.0.en: I say this not for the sake of your own conscience; your conscience does not rebuke or condemn you if you eat of what was sacrificed to an idol, and you are not compelled by your conscience to refrain from eating it, but for the sake of the other, who imagined that eating of it is forbidden. Why should I expose myself to my brother’s blame, as though I were guilty for acting according to my freedom, and cause him to be weakened in his faith and to stumble? He has a right over me that I refrain from causing his conscience to stumble, just as I refrain from what makes my own conscience stumble.

10.27.0.en: God has graciously given me the right to partake of this food, so I have the right to eat and give thanks; but this is not a sufficient reason for me to cause my brother to stumble by eating what he imagines it is not lawful for me to eat, that is, he considers that to be worship and fellowship with idols.

10.28.0.en: This is a rule that every believer must observe in all his words and deeds, so that the purpose of all of them is the glory of God and not his own glory; for this is the chief end of man.

10.29.0.en: Do not cause the Jews to stumble by anything in your dealings with idols, and do not cause the pagans to stumble by encouraging them in anything connected with pagan worship, but do everything that urges them to leave that worship. Likewise with regard to believers who are weak in faith, do not be a cause of their stumbling by your actions, even if those actions are permissible.

10.30.0.en: Before St. Paul asks anything of them, he reminds them that he himself behaves in this way, so that his words are more convincing and acceptable. He never sought to please himself, but did everything that does not conflict with his faith, while at the same time pleasing others, in order to win them to Christ so that they might be saved. Ch. 11:1: So be imitators of me in denying self, in avoiding the causes of stumbling, and in seeking the salvation of souls by every possible means; and I also imitate Christ in His conduct and His teachings, and in this St. Paul is a faithful guide to others.

10.30.1.en: May you be considerate of those around you, and neither say nor do anything that makes them stumble or distracts their minds from God. And you, my sister, take care about the clothes you wear to show your beauty and elegance, without troubling those around you. Let us all remember the value of these souls around us, for they are more precious than anything, since their price is the blood of Christ shed for them.
